current.text: He signed with the Spurs in free agency and replaces Harrison Barnes in the forward rotation.
He has a calf strain. Yahoo lists him as questionable.
His starting spot is not secure. Notes see him as the likely starting power forward, but San Antonio may start Harper, Castle, Vassell and Fox instead.
The Spurs are very deep at guard and forward. The team plans more three-guard lineups.
The Spurs' depth caps his minutes and his fantasy value.
The Spurs are expected to consolidate the roster through trades, but not right away.
The Spurs are projected to be one of the best teams in the West. One expert predicts 63 wins.
His rim finishing fell from 68 percent to 58 percent last season.
His rim finishing might recover in the Spurs offense.
He has limited upside and is not a flyer. Take him late only if you need a steady scorer and rebounder.
He is fair value as a late pick, around pick 142 to 164. Round 14 is the best spot.
His ESPN rank of about 94 and a round 9 or 10 pick are too high. Avoid him at that price.

durable.text: He is a very good defensive rebounder for a forward.
He is a strong isolation and post scorer whom the team can hand the ball to when the offense stalls.
He is streaky from three, but defenses still have to respect his shot.

note: Harris is a 1 USD end-of-draft pick or a waiver player for us. Yahoo values him at 0 USD and ranks him 158, ESPN values him at 3 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. With 144 players drafted, expert calls of pick 142 to 164 put him right on the cutoff. He has no weak category, and his good FT% and low turnovers (z +0.7 and +0.9) let him fill a spot in any build, but nothing in his line moves a category much. Early in the season, check that the calf strain has healed and that he starts at power forward over a three-guard lineup with Harper.
